walkthroughs.body_html:
Changing Urban Areas — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Changing Urban Areas brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Changing Urban Areas.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What are Rio's informal settlements called?
options: Slums
Favelas
Bidonvilles
Townships

mcqs.q: Why do informal settlements develop in rapidly growing LIC cities?
options: People live in slums because they prefer them or are too lazy to find better housing.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
Rural-urban migration outpaces formal housing supply; migrants build their own homes on marginal land without secure land tenure — driven by housing shortage, not by personal choice.

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.

mcqs.q: Why do tropical cyclones only form over warm tropical oceans?
options: Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
Hurricanes form wherever there are strong winds over the sea.
Hurricanes form when two cold fronts collide above the ocean.
They need sea surface temperatures above ~27 degrees C to a depth of 50m to provide energy through evaporation, plus enough Coriolis effect (away from the equator) to spin.
